feedback.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${z}_{1}=4\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $-1.$ Find $f(z).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${z}_{1}=4\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =(-1)(z-4\text{i})(z-(-4\text{i})) \\  & =-(z-4\text{i})(z+4\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(z-4\text{i})(z+4\text{i}) & =-({z}^{2}-(4\text{i})^{2}) \\  & =-({z}^{2}-16{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & =-({z}^{2}+16) \\  & =-{z}^{2}-16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z)=-{z}^{2}-16.$
